## Council question

What is the ordered procedure when multiple factions qualify to win?

## Why this needs a ruling

Quickstart v0.8 removes the tech-token victory contribution first, then Shield Wall if multiple factions still qualify. The recovered JSX uses fractional points to express priority. Infiltration and Bene Gesserit prediction can alter the winners.

## Answer needed

Confirm one ordered winner-resolution procedure covering ordinary strongholds, tech tokens, Shield Wall, alliances, infiltration and prediction. Include a worked simultaneous-qualification example.

## Provisional drafting approach

Prefer an ordered procedure with explicit tests over fractional stronghold values.

This is a research question, not an adopted ruling or a claim that Norbert has answered it. No answer has been supplied yet. Keep the affected rules provisional until Norbert or the council confirms them.

## Sources

Quickstart v0.8, Multiple Win Conditions and infiltration clarifications; recovered Phases.tsx; live [Bene Gesserit](https://dune.zone/factions/bene-gesserit) and [Bene Tleilax](https://dune.zone/factions/bene-tleilax).

Part of #1831. Record the confirmed answer, its date and a worked example here before closing. Norbert will share this link with the council; this ticket does not send them a message.

comments.body:
Partial ruling, confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> BG prediction determination happens AFTER infiltration.
> If BT wins via infiltration, and BG predicted anyone who won, BG steals the victory

Infiltration outcomes are settled in #1849 (one infiltrated ally with 4 strongholds: Bene Tleilax wins with that faction; both infiltrated: Bene Tleilax alone; 5 or more strongholds: infiltration has no effect). Bene Gesserit prediction is then checked against the resulting winners.

**Still open here:** how ordinary strongholds, tech tokens, Shield Wall and alliances are ordered when more than one faction qualifies. In v0.8, the tech-token contribution is removed first, then Shield Wall, if several factions still qualify. Needs confirming, along with whether that comes before infiltration.

---

Confirmed by Norbert on 14 October 2026:

> that order holds, only when there is a tie.
> BT infiltration is not a tie-breaker

**Ordered winner procedure:**
1. **Qualify.** Count each faction's or alliance's strongholds, including tech-token and Shield Wall contributions. Everyone meeting the win condition qualifies.
2. **Break a tie.** Only if more than one faction or alliance qualifies, stop counting the tech-token contribution and re-check. If several still qualify, also stop counting the Shield Wall contribution and re-check.
3. **Infiltration.** Apply Bene Tleilax infiltration to the winning faction or alliance, as in #1849. Infiltration never breaks a tie.
4. **Prediction.** If Bene Gesserit predicted any faction in the final winner set, Bene Gesserit steals the victory.

**Worked example:** at the end of a turn, Harkonnen and Emperor are allied and qualify only because of a tech token. Atreides and Fremen are allied and also qualify. That's a tie, so the tech-token contribution stops counting: Harkonnen–Emperor drop out and Atreides–Fremen win. Bene Tleilax has infiltrated Fremen, and the alliance holds four strongholds, so Bene Tleilax and Fremen win. Bene Gesserit predicted Bene Tleilax, so Bene Gesserit steals the victory.

Closing as answered. The Dream Rulebook draft's victory section still needs this procedure written in; that's a manuscript edit on #1831.
